events.did: Rode in the van with a helmet on and her neck rolled after the van hit a bump
events.quote_anchor: THE van hit a bump, and the back of Rios’s helmet knocked against the armored wall.

events.did: Said from the van wall that they were all dead
events.quote_anchor: And then the EO cuffed to the van’s opposite wall said, “They’re all dead.”

events.did: Said she sees no future for the agents, only death
events.quote_anchor: “No future,” mused the EO sleepily. “Just … dead.”

events.did: Told Rios that in the end all of them meet what is waiting in the mirror, sometimes a what and sometimes a who
events.quote_anchor: In the end, all of us meet what’s waiting in the mirror.” She swallowed dryly. “Most of the time it’s a what. But sometimes it’s a who.”

events.did: Said that this was not how she was going to die
events.quote_anchor: The EO smiled. “Because,” she said, “this isn’t how I die.”

events.did: Found Agent Harris’s office missing from the control room screens and asked guard Tennison where the prisoners from cells three, seven and thirteen were
events.quote_anchor: “Where are the prisoners who were in three, seven, and thirteen?”

events.did: Named Dr. Gray as the answer to what happened to the missing prisoners
events.quote_anchor: “Dr. Gray,” answered the guard, as if that explained everything.

events.did: Walked out of the control room, crossed the gravel lot to her car, started the engine and drove away from EON calmly
events.quote_anchor: She simply crossed the gravel lot to her car, and sank into the driver’s seat, and started the engine, and drove, as calmly as she could

relations.did: Is nineteen years old and, according to her dossier, can see the future in reflective surfaces
relations.quote_anchor: Charlotte Tills. Nineteen. According to the dossier, she could see the future in reflective surfaces.

relations.did: Says humans are one color and EOs another, so their mirrors show a difference
relations.quote_anchor: “Humans are one color, and we’re another. But them.” She tipped her head toward the front of the van.

relations.did: Is the heavyset Black man her team caught, held in the analogue cell fitted for EOs who disrupt technology, and paced the floor measuring it
relations.quote_anchor: In another, an analogue cell, fitted for EOs who tended to disrupt technology, the second one they’d caught, a heavyset Black man named Malcolm

relations.did: Had always been loud to the point of brashness
relations.quote_anchor: Tennison had always been loud to the point of brashness.

numbers.quote_anchor: Charlotte Tills. Nineteen. According to the dossier, she could see the future in reflective surfaces.

numbers.who: the EO targets captured by Rios’s team
numbers.quote_anchor: The mission had been a success. Her team had captured two targets without losing any of their own.

numbers.who: the EOs missing from the cells on the control room screens
numbers.did: Three of the EOs were missing
numbers.quote_anchor: Three of the EOs were missing. She hadn’t noticed, not at first, because two of the three cells weren’t empty.

numbers.who: the cells holding the newly captured EOs
numbers.quote_anchor: She hadn’t noticed, not at first, because two of the three cells weren’t empty.

numbers.who: the cell numbers Rios asked about
numbers.quote_anchor: “Where are the prisoners who were in three, seven, and thirteen?”

numbers.who: the floor where the missing prisoners were taken
numbers.quote_anchor: Sub 1 didn’t hold observation rooms or cells. The only thing located on that floor was the morgue.
